Why It Matters

Evidence You Cannot Get Any Other Way

See Behind Finished Surfaces

Moisture, heat and gaps show up through paint, plaster and tiles

Interpretation, Not Just Pictures

How It Works

4 Stages of a Thermal Survey

A thermal image is only as good as the person interpreting it — that is the real skill

1

Condition Setup

Timing and conditions matter — we survey when the temperature difference will show

2

Systematic Scan

Target areas scanned methodically, with reference images captured alongside

3

Interpretation

Anomalies distinguished from harmless reflections and normal thermal patterns

4

Annotated Report

Thermal and normal images side by side, with temperature data and findings

Applications

5 Things Thermal Imaging Reveals

All of them invisible to the eye, all of them behind a finished surface

Hidden Moisture

Behind walls & ceilings

What Appears
Cool patches where water evaporatesMoisture path outlinedExtent beyond the visible stain
Why It Matters
Shows the true extent — repair scope is often larger than the stain suggests

Electrical Hotspots

DB & circuits under load

What Appears
Overheating terminationsFailing breakersOverloaded cablesLoose connections
Why It Matters
Catches fire risk before failure — the most safety-critical use of thermal

Insulation & Air Gaps

Roof & partition voids

What Appears
Missing insulation sectionsAir leakage pathsUneven roof heat gainPoorly sealed openings
Why It Matters
Explains hot rooms and rising electricity bills

Concealed Pipe Routes

Hot & cold water lines

What Appears
Hot water pipe path tracedLeak point along the runBlocked or dead legsUnderfloor pipe damage
Why It Matters
Locates the pipe before anyone breaks the wall to find it

Debonded Tiles & Voids

Large tiled surfaces

What Appears
Voids behind tilesDebonded renderPattern of hollow areasScreed separation
Why It Matters
Complements tapping tests — maps hollow areas quickly across large surfaces
